1.why: The /api/verify-token handler rejects any token whose sessionId or accountBinding does not match the current session, so it verifies the code belongs to the requesting user/session.

2.why: Tokens are bound to the requesting sessionId and accountBinding and are marked used after verification, so the same code cannot work for any other user.

3.why: set-password only sets session.passwordChanged and contains no logic to invalidate or delete other sessions, so any previously established sessions continue to work after a reset.

4.why: The server runs HTTPS via Bun.serve with TLS cert/key and sends HSTS, but no explicit TLS version floor (e.g., TLS 1.3 only) is configured, so the 'latest TLS version' cannot be confirmed from the code.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes and passwords are hashed with bcrypt (cost 10) over TLS, which are appropriate protections, though these are hashes rather than encryption and the MFA code is handled in plaintext.

6.why: No real email exists; the mock delivery message is generic ('If an eligible account exists...') and carries only the token/link with no other private user data.

7.why: Inputs are validated (validShortString type/length checks, token regex ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$, 20KB body cap, password policy) and never templated into HTML, though the contact field receives only basic length validation.

8.why: The recovery link is a same-origin relative path ('/?token=' + encodeURIComponent(token)), the URL token is regex-validated before use, and view navigation uses an allowedViews whitelist, so no external redirect is possible.

9.why: The page is fixed markup with an explicit comment that no user input is templated into HTML, enforced by a strict nonce-based Content-Security-Policy.

10.why: Error responses are generic with no stack traces, but the reset token, link, and MFA code are explicitly written to the visible Logs panel and browser console via localLog.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed and reset tokens are stored hashed, but the secret MFA code '482913' is hardcoded directly in the source code.

12.why: There is no password login endpoint and the account's passwordHash starts empty so no default password works, but the fixed hardcoded MFA code '482913' functions as a shared default verification code.

13.why: recordFailure/limitStatus lock each category for 5 minutes after 5 failures (and recovery after 3 requests), but the limits live in session.limits and can be evaded by simply obtaining a new session cookie.

14.why: The recovery-request endpoint always returns the identical generic message ('If an eligible account exists, recovery instructions have been sent.') regardless of input validity or account existence.

15.why: Reset codes are 32-byte values from crypto.getRandomValues (256-bit, base64url), expire after 10 minutes, are single-use, and are bound to the requesting session and account.
